measuredFidelity.note: The rig's 6.75-degree leg splay (render.leg-stance) settled ankle daylight at 48.5% against the concept's 46.9%. Round 7 then found that Junebug's SIGNATURE idle pose carried an 8-degree inward leg roll, authored when the rig ran its legs straight down, which closed the ankles to 0.325ft against the bind pose's 0.756 and failed rubric 3.12 in idle while the bind-pose render this command reads stayed correct. The same roll was in all five signature idles and was removed from all of them; an FK sweep now reads every idle within 2% of bind. Re-measured 2026-08-12 after the detector itself was rebuilt to work for the whole roster: the backdrop is now sampled per column (seven sheets are vignetted past the old tolerance), a column counts as occupied by fraction rather than by any single pixel, and the shoe's two tones are read off the concept instead of the hardcoded red/cream that was Junebug's own shoe. Her shoe deltas TIGHTENED, from +2.23/+2.93 under the old classifier to +0.43/-0.78 as tone shares (41.2/25.5 concept against 41.6/24.8 delivered); the round-7 critic note below quotes the old red/cream figures and is left as the record of what was measured then.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read is right and it is right by measurement, not by eye: head 34.0% of figure height against the turnaround's 33.9% (+0.10), head width:height 0.82 against 0.84, ankle daylight 48.5 against 46.9. With colour stripped she is still unmistakably the scowling kid with a bun, a headband and a swept tail. Held off 5 by butt-joined primitives, and I re-observed all three the round-7 critic named, each cropped at 4-10x from the region I cite. (1) BUN/CROWN SHELF, junebug-front-review.png x 220-330 y 55-115: the bun sits on the crown ring with a hard vertical step at BOTH silhouette edges and a shadow line across its base — no fillet, a visible corner, dead centre in the front view. (2) HEADBAND STUB, junebug-profile-review.png x 285-370 y 55-165 at 10x over a magenta backdrop: the band's rear end is a flat-cut rectangle terminating in silhouette against true background, where the concept sweeps it behind the ear to the nape. (3) PONYTAIL TIP, x 290-520 y 40-310: the tail tube ends on a flat circular cut and a separate smaller blob is stuck onto it, the seam a full crease ring with a notch either side, against a concept tip that tapers to a drawn arrowhead. A fourth: the pelvis is a flat-bottomed slab that overhangs the thigh tubes with a hard horizontal ledge across the whole hip, visible on the front board at 4x (x 180-360 y 370-420) and on both profile boards. Nothing is severed — a connected-component pass over all four boards returns exactly one component each.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Child proportion is exact and measured, not asserted: head height delta +0.10 points, head aspect -0.02, ankle daylight +1.61 — every 6b metric inside tolerance, and the head:body read is the turnaround's, never the proxy's. The A-pose boards hold the drawn stance with the arms down and daylight between the thighs and calves, so 3.12 passes on the board and again in the run still. The second clause of the 4 bar — 'joints read as connected forms' — is where it stops. The pelvis-to-thigh is the offender: build_leg's top ring simply terminates at 1.72ft inside a separately built seat, so at 4x on both the front and profile boards you see a slab overhanging a narrower tube with a lip, not a hip. The knee is nearly formless too — the ring table runs 0.180 at the knee against 0.172 just above it, a 5% swell that renders as a straight tapering cylinder in profile. It stays a 4 because the joints that carry motion hold: the run still shows a round deltoid under the sleeve cap, a continuous elbow line and a knee that bends without tearing, and the jersey hem covers the pelvis ledge at every gameplay camera.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The one category below the floor, and the deciding clause is the 4 bar's own words: 'one designed mass'. What ships is four stacked primitives with five visible joins. MEASURED first. Default band (5-45% of head height) reads 1.38 minima/row against the concept's 3.82 — 36% of the strand count at 146% of the prominence. That band is not trustworthy on this kid: on both sheets it spans the headband, whose two edges count as FALSE creases, so I re-ran it on a hair-only band. At 2-14% (bun crest and crown, above the band on both sheets) the concept reads 3.00 minima/row and the delivered reads 0.04 — 1% of the concept's strand count. At 2-22%, 1%. At 2-30%, 8%. The bun is a mathematically featureless dome, which the rubric caps at 4 on its own. Then the joins. (a) The bun butt-joins the crown on a hard shelf with a corner at both silhouette edges (front board 10x, x 220-330 y 55-115) and the toon outline pass draws it as a graphic line at gameplay scale in junebug-runtime-hero.png. (b) The hair tie is a FLAT QUAD SLAB, not a wrap: at 10x over magenta it is a single plane crossing in front of the tail whose lower edge is a hard flat cut with true background beneath it, and at gameplay scale in the run still it reads as a yellow tab stuck to the side of the head. (c) True background — alpha 0, sampled at (310,72) and (315,80) of junebug-profile-review.png — shows through the notch between the bun and the ponytail root, so the two masses do not touch; the tail hangs off the head through a narrow neck below the tie. (d) The tip blob. The 4 clauses it does pass are real and worth saying: the hairline is a proper sculpted widow's-peak that reads clean against skin from the front, there is no bare-skull read from any angle, and the headband arch itself is the best-authored accessory on the sheet.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The strongest sculpted category. Garments read as constructed at 5x on the A-pose board: the V-collar is a rounded piping TUBE rather than a painted line, the placket carries three raised button studs, the sleeves have two white stripes plus a real white cuff band, the belt is a band with two loops and a buckle, the knicker gathers into a darker cuff, the sock has its own band, and the shoe has a distinct lighter midsole slab and a red toe cap. The shoe's split is measured, not eyeballed: dominant tone 63.7% of the band against the concept's 64.7, second tone 31.1 against 27.2, mean saturation 34.9 against 36.8. Off 5 on the laces, which are three raised rectangular slabs on the vamp — they do not cross, have no eyelets and no weave, and on the right shoe of the front board one slab breaks the shoe's silhouette (x 160-390 y 590-710 at 4x). Secondary: the jersey hem is a flat horizontal slab cut with square corners rather than a hem that falls over the hip.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The face is a FORM, and I checked the specific things that separate a form from a sticker. A real nose breaks the profile with a defined tip and a nostril underside (junebug-profile-review.png x 210-320 y 110-240 at 8x). No decal-island seam anywhere — I looked for one at 8-10x on both the front and the profile and the atlas wraps the cheek and temple planes continuously. The ears are the best-constructed detail on the whole model: outer helix rim, inner concha shadow, and a lobe sitting against the skull, which settles 3.10 with no ambiguity. Features are legible at hero scale and the angled scowl brows still read at 40px. The chest patch I thought was a texture island at 4x is a specular gradient — resolved at 10x, not a defect. Held off 5 by the mouth. At rest it is a thin flat stroke a few pixels tall, close to the 'collapses to a line' the rubric warns about, and the expression RANGE does not survive: I pixel-diffed a 46x36 mouth box across the four runtime stills and grin/cheer/tongue are the same mouth (grin vs cheer 99 of 4968 channels differ by more than 12, max 39; cheer vs tongue 202, max 70) while only angry is distinct (650-669, max 120). Cropping the source atlas confirms it is the asset, not the capture instrument: cells 1, 10 and 11 are three near-identical open smiles, so the tongue cell has no tongue out and the cheer cell is no wider than the grin. All four stills are genuinely painted — byte sizes 291673/291988/292081/292276, a 0.2% spread, and all four show grass, sky and the character.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity survives both ends. At hero (junebug-runtime-hero.png, devstats reads 'model model', so this is the delivered GLB and not proxy evidence) the read is complete: scowl brows, big eyes, white headband arch, dark bun, tail swept to her left. I generated my own 40px read by resizing the front board to 40px tall, and every load-bearing element holds — dark bun over a white band, red top, pink pants, red socks, white shoes, and the angled brows are still two dark marks that say 'determined'. Off 5 on two counts. First, in the FRONT view at field scale the ponytail is entirely hidden behind her, so at 40px she is a bun-and-headband kid and the signature tail — the thing the turnaround draws an arrow at — contributes nothing to the read from the camera the fielder is most often seen from. Second, the tie reads at hero as a flat yellow tab rather than a wrap (junebug-runtime-run.png x 415-595 y 140-290 at 6x), which is a hero-scale accessory defect, not a hair-only one.

priorHumanReview.verdict: approved — reviewed the shipped model in production at https://srgirsky.github.io/recess-sports/ after rounds 5-7 rebuilt the shoe as one lasted upper, reshaped the ear, deepened the run's arm swing, mirrored the face columns and restored the splayed stance in every signature idle. The six category scores recorded here are the round-7 independent critic's, not the sculptor's.

The jersey hem is a flat horizontal slab cut with square corners rather than a hem that falls over the hip.

NOT a defect, recorded so the next critic does not re-report it: the pale quad on the chest visible at 4x resolves at 10x as a specular gradient, not a texture-island seam. Ears are fully constructed (rim, concha shadow, lobe) and are the best detail on the model — EarSpec/build_ear are imported from sculptlib. The near-side eye in the profile board is foreshortened, which is correct for a true orthographic 90-degree view. All four runtime-face stills are painted.

Sources confirm ten lock spines (three mirrored pairs + two centre + one mid pair), 7-sided tubes, sweep authored in +y with side-lock tips at x ±0.61/±0.44.
measuredFidelity.note: featurelatitude gates brow 56.2, eye 71.6 (bounded crop traces), mouth 83.5 (the analyser's own trace). polishFindings: PRIMARY. The chair is half the mass the sheet gives it and sits too low on the figure: measured 43.6% lower-40% fill against the concept's 83.7%, chair top 61.1% down against 44.9%, chair width 43.4% of figure height against ~60%. Raise the seat/wheel assembly relative to the hip so the wheel tops reach his elbow as they do on the sheet, and thicken the seat, backrest and rails until the front board's lower half is a dense black-and-blue mass rather than open scaffolding. Everything else on this list is downstream of it. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

The drive wheels read as flat parallel-sided black slabs with square-cut faceted ends in the front board, not as cambered ellipses. The camber is authored (WHEEL_CAMBER 0.115) but at 16 ring points and a 0.060 tube it does not survive the orthographic front view. Either increase the camber or give the tyre enough ring points that the lean reads as a curve. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

The four frame rails per side terminate in tapered points hanging in mid-air (rail 1 ends at z 0.300, radius 0.036, i.e. z 0.264 with ground at 0) and cross in an unresolved X in the front board. Close the chassis: join the rails into axle bosses and a caster fork so no tube ends in space. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

The METAL footplate ellipsoid is buried inside the WHITE sole tube (sole bottom z 0.343 vs footplate top z 0.423) and pokes out through the outboard side of the sneaker as a bare grey stub at hero scale - a 3.8 interpenetration. The caster is an open torus (ring radius 0.130, tube radius 0.040) so the field shows through its middle at hero scale. The sheet's caster is a solid small wheel with a blue hub - fill the centre. [CARRIED VERBATIM - chair out of scope this round]

polishFindings: CLEARED 3.2 (knee half) — the knee now reads as a cap and hollow at 1x. peaches-front-review.png (150,440 240x240 at 1x, 200,480 140x130 at 5x, 215,500 50x70 at 10x): each leg widens to 36 px at the kneecap (board y520-528) over a 31 px hollow (y536), a 14% step that reads as a joint without magnification; the contour through cap and hollow is a smooth S with no ring seam, step or facet. In profile (peaches-profile-review.png 220,480 90x140 at 6x) the same rings measure 36 over 32 px. In motion: the run's bent front knee (peaches-runtime-run.png 560,470 120x110 at 5x) bends as one smooth surface with the cap riding the bend, and the trailing straight leg (400,480 120x120 at 5x) shows the knee as a soft kink with no crease or tear; swing (470,520 140x180), idle (face-angry 450,520 160x150) and hero (460,520 140x160) at 4x all show the knee. No see-through anywhere at the knee.

CLEARED 3.2 (calf/ankle half) — the taper is in the silhouette. Profile contour from hem to sock: 34 -> 36 (kneecap) -> 32 (hollow) -> 36 (calf, y549 = z ~0.70) -> 28 (ankle, y565) -> 32 (sock roll): a 22% narrowing from calf to ankle where the hair round had a flat 32 -> 30 -> 32. Front: 35 (calf) -> 29 (ankle) -> 33 (sock roll). At 1x (150,440 240x240 on both boards) the leg reads as a leg with a calf and an ankle, not a pipe. Thigh:ankle 35:29 = 1.2 against the sheet's ~1.3 — close enough that the difference is not a finding.

NEW minor — the knee and calf are radially symmetric, so the profile reads as a turned baluster. peaches-profile-review.png (220,480 90x140 at 6x): the kneecap bulges the BACK contour by the same +2 px as the front (both sides 252-287.5 at y521-529 vs 253-286.5 above), the hollow pinches both sides, and the calf swells the FRONT of the shin as much as the back. The sheet's profile (turnaround 800,560 160x150) is an asymmetric S — kneecap forward at the knee, calf bulge behind the shin, a straight shin bone in front. _with_knee scales the ring's half-width; the leg ring would need a forward (-y) centre offset at the cap and a rearward offset at the calf to read as anatomy from the side. At 1x the profile leg now reads 'shaped' rather than 'pipe', which is why this is minor and not a carry of 3.2.

NEW cosmetic — the toon outliner traces the ribbing. peaches-runtime-face-angry.png (450,520 160x150 at 4x) and peaches-runtime-swing.png (470,520 140x180 at 4x): both the inner and outer outline of each leg are now wavy through the knee-calf-ankle band. It reads as a leg with a knee at 1x; at 4x it has a faint ribbed-tube quality. Follows directly from the symmetric rings above; the asymmetry fix would settle it too.

CLEARED 3.11 (carried from the deltoid round, re-checked on the fresh boards) — the deltoid fairs into the sleeveless arm: no shadow crease under it and no hard outboard step on peaches-front-apose-review.png (190,240 / 290,240 70x70 at 8x); no pocket or see-through at the armpit. Residual minor: the toon outliner still draws a short crease tick under the dome in idle, run and hero (face-angry 455,300 150x80 at 5x) — the outline pass catching the 0.004 ft step where the dome sits proud of the 0.090 ring; cosmetic.

CARRIED 3.5 BLOCKER — decal-island seam on the face. peaches-front-review.png (195,130 60x80) at 8x: the lighter flat forehead patch meets darker skin along a two-step staircase at the upper-left hairline; (300,140 50x80) at 8x: a straight vertical seam at the right temple with a squared corner below the hairline. At runtime peaches-runtime-face-angry.png (455,190 150x90) at 5x shows the same lighter patch, a squared notch upper-right, and darker skin strips between the patch and the hair on both sides — visible at 1x in every face still. FACE_ISLAND (0.92, -1.6924, 2.500) is in the source; the island exists and is mis-shaded, not missing.

CARRIED 3.3 — the bun's STEP SEAM ring. peaches-front-review.png (215,110 110x45) at 8x: a hard horizontal crease where BUN_LEVELS' bottom ring (z 3.580, half 0.160) lands on the cap crown, the bun overhanging it; peaches-profile-review.png (220,120 120x50) at 8x: the bun sits as a separate dome on a lit cap shelf. The bun's base is narrower than the cap top it sits on, so the two masses never merge.

CARRIED 3.3 — the bun is no longer an acorn at 1% (measure:strands 24% at 222%), but at peaches-runtime-hero.png (470,160 120x90) at 6x it reads as a faceted walnut — broad diagonal facets with two or three darker bands, no wrap direction, no coil; at peaches-front-review.png (200,70 140x80) at 5x, a smooth acorn with faint dimpling. The sheet's bun is a coil of ~8 twisted ropes with a visible wrap. The source ships BUN_SEEDS amplitude=0.055 with HAIR_TROUGH bun valleys; only the cap's troughs take HAIR_DEEP.

CARRIED 3.8 — the temple wisps cross the ears in the front view. peaches-front-review.png (285,155 60x60) at 8x: the dark-brown wisp tube lies directly across the tan ear, whose top and lobe protrude above and below it; mirrored on the left. Geometry: the tube runs at y -0.28..-0.30, forward of the ear centre (y 0.020), so this is a fat tube (radius 0.062 at x 0.385) OCCLUDING the ear in front projection, not interpenetration — the fix is a thinner wisp dropped below the ear line, where the sheet hangs it beside the cheek.

CARRIED 3.4 — no bodice straps, scoop or armhole binding. peaches-front-review.png (190,250 160x250) at 3x: a truncated cone with one cream ring at its top; the bare arm exits the cone's side with no edge. grep of sculpt-peaches-source.py: 'straps' appears only in PEACHES_SHOE and 'scoop'/'armhole' nowhere — the bodice binding is ABSENT, not misbuilt; it needs a builder, not a tune.

CARRIED 3.4 — the leaf appliqué is a blob. builder.ellipsoid((0.200,-0.330,1.360),(0.070,0.022,0.120),TRIM). peaches-front-review.png (270,420 50x60) at 8x: a featureless pale teardrop with no outline and no vein, roughly a third of the width the sheet gives the leaf (sheet front 230,470 60x100). At runtime (face-angry 410,300 250x390) it is a small cream chip at the right hip. Misbuilt/undersized, present.

CARRIED 6b.2 — the sneaker reads cream, not peach. Measured: second tone 63.0% vs 47.5% (+15.5, tol 8), mean saturation 27.4 vs 32.7 (-5.30, tol 4). peaches-front-review.png (190,570 160x90) at 4x: the peach SHOE #F0A878 survives only as a patch on the outer quarter; cupsole, toe bumper and the tongue/vamp are all cream. The source's shoe comments still say 'green canvas' — the band split was tuned for another kid's template and not re-tuned for peach vs cream.

CARRIED 6b.4 — stance, not tolerance. Ankle daylight 34.0 vs the sheet's 0.00 (tol 12); peaches-front-review.png legs stand parallel with clear daylight from thigh to sock where the sheet stands feet together. Do not widen the tolerance.

CARRIED minor (was part of 3.2) — the neck is a plain cylinder above the collar ring (peaches-profile-review.png 240,235 40x40 at 4x). The sheet's neck is short and mostly hidden by the collar, so this is a silhouette-transition note (3.1), not a proportion finding.

CARRIED minor — the ear reads as a claw in profile. peaches-profile-review.png (250,160 70x70) at 8x: the ear is a tan crescent with a sharp upward spike at its front and a hooked point at its back, both cutting into the cap's lower edge, with a dark shadowed underside — a two-pronged claw, not the sheet's rounded helix and lobe (sheet profile 830,230 60x70). build_ear/EAR_SPEC (line 140) is present; the rim spikes and the cap fringe notch around it are what need softening. Rubric 3.10.

CARRIED minor — the profile nose is a thorn. peaches-profile-review.png (205,195 30x30) at 4x: nose_push's tip (0.094, across**1.25) renders as a sharp isosceles spike off the face plane where the sheet draws a tiny rounded button. It does break the profile, but it reads as a beak at hero scale.

NON-DEFECT (cropped) — the dashed dark trail at the armpit in peaches-runtime-swing.png (530,345 55x55) at 8x is the toon outline of the arm-root ring continuing a few pixels inboard along the dress; the dress colour is continuous behind it, no hole. Cosmetic outline fragment; still present.

NON-DEFECT (cropped) — a black diagonal sliver on the medial forefoot of each shoe on the front board (peaches-front-review.png 200,600 60x50 at 10x) sits inside a rounded lighter panel above a continuous cupsole; it is the unlit interior of an open lace loop seen edge-on, not a hole to background. At runtime (face-angry 450,600 170x80) the same loop draws as a hooked outline squiggle. Cosmetic.

CARRIED polish — no freckles and no blush anywhere on the delivered face (all four runtime face stills, 450,150 160x170); the sheet carries both across the cheeks and nose bridge (sheet front 150,290 130x60). grep of sculpt-peaches-source.py for 'freckle' and 'blush' returns nothing — absent from the sculpt; if they live in the face atlas they are not reaching the render.

NON-DEFECT Trap-3 — TEAM_MASK is the raw grey ring on both socks on the boards (front-review 220,585 and 300,585, ~14px tall) and tints pale in the team colour at runtime (hero 500,580). It is confined to the two leg-loft stations at z 0.425/0.390 and its EXTENT matches the sheet's single thin sock stripe. Judged by extent only.
NON-DEFECT Trap-4 — the dark slit at the near eye in peaches-profile-review.png (225,170) is the near-side eye foreshortened in true orthographic profile. Not a defect.

PASSES verified on the fresh evidence — nothing is severed; legs are two legs with daylight between thighs and calves in bind pose (front 200,480 140x130), A-pose (front-apose 200,480 140x130), idle (face-angry 450,520) and run (run 380,430 340x230); the larger knee amount and the two new station widths introduced no seam, step, facet or see-through at rest or mid-clip; the 40-px strip shows a continuous figure; the face is visible in the front board; run and swing stills show no torn elbow, shoulder or knee. Evidence freshness checked: boards and runtime stills 03:54-03:55 today, kid_peaches.glb and peaches-pilot.blend 03:54, checked at 03:55.
